findings.description: SYS-SUP-003 detects a late-start fault when a task starts late but sets no detection deadline. CON-SUP-105 measures the safe-state reaction from expiry of a timing limit; OP-SYS-010 leaves detection of a task that never starts unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-010 as blocking and resolve the detection rule and deadline for a task that has not started.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-003 accepts a start at the limit and rejects a later start, but CON-SUP-103 specifies 100 µs measurement resolution. OP-SYS-009 leaves classification of starts in the measurement step containing the limit unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-009 as blocking and resolve the late-start boundary classification.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-013 requires watchdog service to be withheld only after both fault-report transmission and safe-state entry complete. It leaves service between detection of a task fault and that point unspecified, although STK-SUP-005 permits service only while every supervised task is healthy. OP-SYS-011 records the conflict with completing the fault reactions before a watchdog reset.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the watchdog service rule and its interaction with fault reporting and safe-state entry, then specify the resulting behavior.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-014 relies on a stored reference for the program-code check, but OP-SYS-004 leaves the reference and comparison method undefined. The expected detection of changes to the application image cannot be established.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-004 as blocking and resolve the integrity-check acceptance criteria.

findings.description: CON-SUP-112 requires milliseconds since start, but OP-SYS-006 leaves the timestamp origin and wrap behavior undefined. Expected report values across resets and counter wrap cannot be determined.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-006 as blocking and resolve the timestamp origin and wrap behavior.

findings.description: OP-SYS-005 leaves the status state values and the meaning of fault count undefined, so the expected GET STATUS response cannot be determined for a given operating and reset history.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-005 as blocking and resolve the state values and fault-count semantics.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-004 requires detection at expiry while accepting completion at that instant. OP-SYS-009 leaves treatment of a completion in the same 100 µs measurement step as expiry unspecified, preventing a boundary verdict.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-009 as blocking and resolve the execution-limit boundary classification.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-003 detects a late-start fault only when the task starts, while CON-SUP-105 measures the reaction from expiry of a timing limit. OP-SYS-010 defers the detection instant for a task that never starts, leaving its timely response unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-010 as blocking and specify the detection and reaction timing for a task that has not started.

findings.description: SYS-SUP-024 requires an entity in every fault report, but SYS-SUP-026 omits the entity for code 4. CON-SUP-104 permits missing or out-of-order checkpoints involving more than one task, and OP-SYS-012 records that the entity-selection rule is undecided.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the entity-selection rule for flow faults and specify it in the requirements.
